name: Dhaka Medical College Students
contribution: Students of Dhaka Medical College helped organize resistance, shelter wounded demonstrators, and build the first temporary Shaheed Minar after the 21 February 1952 killings.
context: The Medical College hostel and its surrounding streets were a crucial protest, treatment, and mourning zone during the Language Movement. Students worked alongside demonstrators and medical staff under intense state pressure.
impact: Their actions turned a site of violence into a place of collective mourning and memory. The group represents the practical, medical, and organizational labour that sustained the movement after the shootings.
highlight: Dhaka Medical College students who sheltered the wounded and built the first temporary Shaheed Minar.
seoTitle: Dhaka Medical College Students and the 1952 Movement
seoDescription: Learn how Dhaka Medical College students sheltered the wounded and built the first Shaheed Minar after the 1952 Language Movement killings.
shortAnswer: Dhaka Medical College students helped organize resistance, care for wounded protesters, and build the first temporary Shaheed Minar in 1952.

faq.question: What did Dhaka Medical College students do in 1952?
faq.answer: They helped organize resistance, shelter wounded demonstrators, and build the first temporary Shaheed Minar after the 21 February killings.
